concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: On 15 September 2026, the amendment had been signed but its breach-notification change was not yet effective. The original provision therefore required notification without undue delay and no later than 48 hours.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment's replacement breach-notification clause took effect on 1 October 2026 and requires notification no later than 24 hours after the Processor becomes aware of a breach.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduced the routine on-site audit notice period from 30 days to 20 days. The 10-Business-Day period in the annex does not override the amendment's main body.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: By 1 November 2026, the amended liability clause set the Processor's aggregate cap at EUR 1,000,000. This fixed cap applies regardless of the EUR 700,000 in fees paid during the preceding 12 months.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amended liability clause expressly states that the EUR 1,000,000 cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality obligations.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd was listed as an approved Sub-processor, and its approval was not withdrawn until 1 January 2027. It was therefore approved on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The amendment expressly withdrew Meridian Mail Ltd's approval with effect from 1 January 2027, so it was not approved on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, Personal Data was stored or processed in Norway, Estonia, Ireland, Lithuania, France, and Denmark, yielding six distinct countries.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: The amended return-and-deletion period was 60 days after termination. Counting 60 calendar days from the 31 December 2026 termination gives 1 March 2027 as the latest date.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. the notice must include specified information about the breach and its response, and the processor must document breaches and cooperate with required regulatory or data-subject communications.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The notice must include specified information about the breach and its response, and the Processor must document breaches and cooperate with required regulatory or data-subject communications.
justifications: The amended notification clause establishes the 24-hour outer deadline, while the unchanged provisions specify the notice contents, breach documentation, and cooperation duties.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The breach involved confirmed exposure of usable privileged credentials, triggering the expedited 12-hour outer notification limit.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April, making the 12-hour deadline 05:10 on 10 April; the first notice at 06:00 was 50 minutes late.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The third Business Day after awareness is reached on 16 April because 14 April was an approved full-day pause; the report is due by the end of that day.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 60 days after termination, but the records remain held until the later hold ends on 25 August. The tenth Business Day after release is 9 September, which is later than the ordinary deadline.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deletion deadline and 35 calendar days after creation. Thirty-five calendar days after its 30 June creation date is 4 August, earlier than the 60-day ordinary deadline.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained solely under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation. The requested analytics use was rejected and no other authorization applies.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval began on the latest of the proposed start date, written consent, and completed security review: 22 April 2027.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS remained approved for ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd was withdrawn and its emergency permission did not cover ordinary customer email.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: Actual processing with effective authorisation existed in Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France, and Sweden on 15 May 2027. Denmark was withdrawn, Finland and Germany lacked the required conditions, and Ireland's emergency permission had expired.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,140,000 after excluding VAT, the service credit, the one-off training fee, and event-month fees. Twice that amount is EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 minimum security cap.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000, reduced by EUR 300,000 in earlier ordinary payments during the same Contract Year, leaving EUR 700,000.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: The payable amounts are EUR 700,000 for the ordinary claim, EUR 1,750,000 for the single duplicated security loss, and EUR 350,000 for the two confidentiality losses, totaling EUR 2,800,000. The security amount is within the EUR 1,780,000 remaining security pool, while confidentiality losses are uncapped.
